name: Patrick Enright
title: Senior Creative Producer
summary: Senior creative producer and U.S. Navy veteran with 14 years in brand identity, graphic design, video and photography production, UX/UI, web, and live events. Led in-house creative for a venture-backed technology company through more than 20 contract wins and a raise of more than $4 million, owning everything from brand and sales collateral to app and website UX. Works closely with engineers and specialists to understand complex systems and explain them so any audience can follow.

bullets.text: Delivered more than 20 design, photo, and video projects, including brand identities, logotypes, look books, motion graphics, websites, print, and social media assets for clients across a variety of industries (government, food and beverage, entertainment, tech, medical).
Built Contrast Bench, a color tool that checks palettes against WCAG and APCA accessibility standards, as an Adobe Illustrator plug-in and a web app.
Supported photo shoots for live music events and edited B-roll and photography for clients including iHeartRadio and Google.
Real estate marketing service: video walkthroughs, 360-degree tours, photography, and listing websites.

Designed pitch decks and sales materials targeting organizations across the private and public sectors, supporting more than 20 multimillion-dollar contracts, including one Navy Program of Record, and helping raise more than $4 million in venture capital.

Built accessibility-first design systems for three products, structured for AI coding tools, enabling engineering teams to quickly prototype features across platforms at about 90% brand compliance from the first prompt.
Designed UX/UI for six apps, including a virtual reality app, creating every on-screen element and icon by hand, taking cues from Material Design and Apple Human Interface Guidelines.

Ran usability tests with active-duty Marines during live exercises at Marine Corps Air Station Yuma, building a feedback loop that turned their input into design fixes within days, and later within 24 hours.

Directed creative and production for five virtual and in-person conferences with more than 3,700 total attendees, including live broadcast graphics, camera operation, promotional and documentary video, web design, event photography, site surveys, and show scripts.
Worked directly with engineering teams as the code-to-design bridge and regularly collaborated with and briefed CEOs, admirals, and generals on creative and product work.

Led and mentored a two-person team of graphic design and marketing professionals, plus rotating interns, to execute ad campaigns and support design needs for social media calendars across earned and owned media.
Produced more than 50 videos for product showcases, live events, recruiting, training, and sales, growing YouTube subscribers 500% in two years.
Designed and maintained more than 10 websites using React/Tailwind or Webflow and optimized SEO, reaching No. 1 on Google for targeted search terms.

Created digital and print collateral (brand identity, social ads, typefaces, templates, illustrations, animations, videos) for two subsidiary tech startups, 11 technology product lines, and recruiting campaigns that supported more than 75 hires.

Designed the branding and website for Project Convergence 2020, an internationally recognized Department of Defense event, with the branding still in use for the annual event involving all five branches of the U.S. military and allied nations.
Produced a new branding suite with a range of design assets (responsive logo marks, style guides, and templates) using Illustrator, improving marketing efforts toward small-business partners.
Produced, shot, and edited videos supporting command messaging, including a four-part documentary and three recorded soldier touchpoint events with more than 24,000 views.
Created digital and print design products for 20 PR initiatives with up to 2,000 attendees, producing branding for internal and community-wide programs with public figures in attendance.
Captured and edited photos for more than 20 public events with distinguished guests for historical preservation.
Promoted to E-6, a supervisory grade, in 4.5 years.

Shot video for the documentary “Boot Camp: Making a Sailor” (2018), achieving more than 10 million views and a regional Emmy nomination in the Documentary, Cultural/Topical category (National Capital Chesapeake Bay chapter).
Led 22 sailors as lead petty officer, giving first-line editorial approval on All Hands video, photo, and written products.
Edited more than 10 issues of All Hands, the Navy's flagship magazine, laying out and designing content from a 20-person team of sailors and civilian staff.

Served as on-camera talent for a STEM virtual field trip filmed at Space and Naval Warfare Systems Center Pacific and broadcast to classrooms nationwide, earning praise from the chief of naval operations.
Authorized final release and copy-edited articles on Navy.mil for 300 writers, reviewing more than 140 submissions weekly.
Produced more than 70 stories of U.S. Navy sailors through photography, video, and feature writing for online channels, including magazines and social media, achieving around 30,000 views on YouTube.

Orchestrated marketing and PR ship tours with a six-person team for 488 distinguished visitors, including then-Vice President Joe Biden, Justice Anthony Kennedy, and other leaders from the public and private sectors; the program won the Navy's Thompson-Ravitz Award for Community Outreach (Afloat Large) in 2015 and 2016.

Managed a cross-functional team of more than 20 sailors and over $35,000 in inventory and equipment for the ship's only print shop, delivering production needs (design, print, video) for more than 6,000 crew members.

Designed and produced the 400-page 2016 deployment cruise book: coordinated portraits of 5,500 sailors, organized the files by division, and automated the layout, earning third place for best large-command cruise book in the Navy's 2016 Russell Egnor Navy Media Awards.

Designed the command's website and submitted work (websites, stories, newspapers) to Navy-wide media competitions, earning Outstanding New Graphic Artist (2014), second place for best Navy website (2015), and 10 more Russell Egnor Navy Media Awards.
Oversaw publication of a weekly newspaper and a biweekly magazine, ensuring 100% on-time delivery.
